care_problem: keeping older or disabled people at home instead of higher-cost institutional settings
control_point: caregiver labor state density personal care hospice home health and managed-care relationships
payer: Medicaid managed care hospice home-health payers patients and families
main_burden_carrier: caregivers wage inflation compliance state rates branches and acquisition integration
current_evidence: FY2025 revenue 1.42B; Q2 2026 revenue 377.4M; OCF 40.0M; personal care 78.4%; hospice 17.0%; home health 4.6%
qoe_or_shenanigans_test: test caregiver hours wages retention overtime agency use rates denials acquisitions compliance and recoupments
owner_cash_denominator: cash after wages branches compliance acquisitions maintenance capital taxes debt leases and dilution
valuation_and_macro_boundary: price must assume local density and sustainable reimbursement; stress wages rates government budgets labor shortage and liquidity
thesis_breaker: caregiver supply or reimbursement fails to cover wages while acquisitions add volume without profitable density

care_problem: repeated kidney-failure treatment and integrated chronic-care management
control_point: treatment density clinics staffing payer mix home modality and risk-based kidney care
payer: government and commercial payers and patients through healthcare financing
main_burden_carrier: clinical labor centers supplies reimbursement compliance and medical-cost risk
current_evidence: FY2025 revenue 13.643B; operating income 2.044B; Q2 2026 OCF 490M; about 91650 US treatments per day; about 5.8B annualized medical spend in risk arrangements
qoe_or_shenanigans_test: split treatment volume from reimbursement and medical-cost risk; test labor supplies center utilization reserves and risk outcomes
owner_cash_denominator: cash after center maintenance supplies clinical labor risk-based medical costs debt taxes capital needs and common claims
valuation_and_macro_boundary: price must assume recurring treatment and manageable risk; stress reimbursement wages government policy rates and medical costs
thesis_breaker: treatment or risk volume grows while reimbursement labor supplies or medical-cost risk compresses cash

care_problem: recurring specialty infusion moved from hospital to home or alternate sites
control_point: national infusion workforce pharmacy payer contracts therapy breadth logistics and authorization
payer: payers manufacturers providers and patients or families
main_burden_carrier: nurses pharmacists drug acquisition authorization supplies service intensity and reimbursement
current_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue 1.442B; adjusted EBITDA 117.5M; Q1 revenue 1.3507B; adjusted EBITDA 104.8M; Q4 2025 revenue up 8.8%
qoe_or_shenanigans_test: test therapy mix drug cost rebates inventory denials nurse capacity payer settlement and adjusted-to-GAAP cash
owner_cash_denominator: cash after drug and supply costs clinical labor authorization branches sites taxes debt and dilution
valuation_and_macro_boundary: price must assume site-of-care conversion and service margin; stress payer cuts drug inflation nurse scarcity rates and hospital competition
thesis_breaker: site-of-care growth slows or therapy mix reimbursement and service intensity consume expected margin

care_problem: coordinating pharmacy and provider services around complex patients
control_point: pharmacy plus provider workflows national reach patient density and recurring coordination
payer: payers government programs patients referral sources and facilities
main_burden_carrier: clinicians pharmacists labor drug pricing reimbursement leverage and integration
current_evidence: more than 465000 patients daily; about 43M prescriptions in 2025; Q2 2026 revenue 3.873B; gross profit 492.7M; adjusted EBITDA 205.5M; home-health census 46448
qoe_or_shenanigans_test: test prescription and patient volume versus collections drug cost labor reimbursement integration leverage and GAAP cash
owner_cash_denominator: cash after pharmacy provider labor integration leverage working capital capex taxes and common claims
valuation_and_macro_boundary: price must assume coordination improves retention and margin; stress drug prices labor reimbursement rates leverage and government budgets
thesis_breaker: volume rises without EBITDA-to-cash conversion or leverage reimbursement labor and integration overwhelm coordination benefits
